newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 20.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Friday:

* The Senate's package of Medicare revisions is not being embraced by members of the U.S. House of Representatives who object to two cornerstones of the legislation: to raise the Medicare eligibility age to 67 from 65 and to increase payments by affluent elderly.
* In the era of "Just Say No" to drugs, the drug culture continues to flourish over the Internet, where information on drug use is prevalent and easy to find.
* The White House was growing edgy about the potential political ramifications as prospects of a tobacco settlement grow near.

* The U.S., the host to this weekend's summit meeting of the world's industrial leaders, is experiencing a robust economy. But don't expect other countries to try to model their economies after the United States.

* McDonald's Corp won a libel case and a $96,000 judgment against two activists who accused the fast-food giant of a myriad of transgressions, from destroying rain forests to poisoning customers, which were found untrue by a British judge.
* The woman who pressed rape charges against Alex Kelly of Darien, Conn., goes public for the first time since he was convicted, saying she hopes the 11 years of nightmares are finally over.
